fact: The Ministry of Finance reports that rollout of PFM Smart, a web-based and real-time accounting system replacing the councils' ex-post Petra application, was complete at Freetown City Council, with all transactions from January 2025 in the system and transactions processed live with payment instructions printed from it; the statement is undated within a report on January to June 2025, and the report does not say how the council is connected.

One local council of 22, Freetown City Council, was working live in the web-based PFM Smart system in the Ministry of Finance's report on January to June 2025, with five more councils planned before the end of 2025 and all 22 by 2026; the one council is the capital city.

The World Bank's Sierra Leone Digital Transformation Project has an activity to provide last-mile broadband access to selected public institutions, named as ministries, departments and agencies, local government offices, hospitals and health clinics, and schools, in Freetown and in secondary cities that have no broadband; its feasibility study had been started by the implementation support mission of April 2025.

The World Bank counts 50 public institutions connected to broadband internet under the project at 28 July 2025, unchanged from 13 January 2025, against a target of 300 by June 2027; the count covers ministries, local government offices, health facilities and schools together and gives no figure for local government offices.

The last-mile connectivity activity sits in Component 1 of the Sierra Leone Digital Transformation Project, costed at USD 21.3 million of a USD 50 million World Bank IDA grant (IDA-E1130), of which 21.24 per cent was disbursed at 24 August 2025; no domestic budget line is stated.

A readiness assessment of seven councils (Bo, Bonthe, Kenema, Koidu New-Sembehun, Makeni, Port Loko and Western Area Rural District) for the World Bank-financed Resilient Urban Sierra Leone Project found internet connectivity in the municipalities relatively good but still reached through individually provided internet modems; the report is undated and takes its month from the World Bank's document number.

Of the seven councils assessed, all outside Freetown, the report names none with a connection provided to the council, stating that the internet is reached through individually provided modems and that supporting network, hardware and software are insufficient; it gives no total of councils, and the month is taken from the World Bank's document number.

In the seven councils assessed, internal data is shared by USB stick, by email and from other workstations, and outside data is fetched from its producers on written request by the same means; officials of Bo, Makeni, Port Loko, Bonthe and Western Area Rural District named reliable or uninterrupted internet connectivity among the resources they still need. The report is undated and takes its month from the World Bank's document number.
